close_reason: Already delivered by bedrock-ghd (PR #215, commit 328efbb5). The ticket asks that LocalFilesystem.put/4 stop writing straight onto the target path and instead write a temp file in the same directory and rename onto it. develop does exactly that: put/4 calls write_scratch/2, which opens .bedrock-tmp.<key>.<node>.<pid>.<n> with :exclusive, writes, syncs, then :file.rename onto the key, with discard_scratch/2 on failure. S3 needed no change, as the ticket said. Open PR #305 is a different defect (unlocked read-compare-rename in put_if_version_matches) and leaves the scratch protocol intact. Dependency on bedrock-wxf.6.7 removed; no residual work.
description:
LocalFilesystem.put/4 is File.write straight onto the target path, so it truncates in place and a concurrent reader can observe a partially written object.

The exposure is limited today because production writes go through put_if_not_exists/4, which opens with :exclusive and so never touches an existing object. Consolidation overwrites live keys, which makes the torn read reachable.

Write to a temporary file in the same directory and rename onto the target. S3 is already atomic per object and needs no change.
title: LocalFilesystem.put writes via temp file and rename
